feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by useful scale indicators. It is clear and well-written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and a few style/grammar inconsistencies reduce polish.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support leadership in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications.  
- Good credibility signals: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact and specificity.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: combines strategy, technical execution, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that fits public-sector digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” and “communications operations” recur across summary, competencies, and roles. Consolidating would sharpen impact.  
- Tighten structure: the CV has overlapping sections (“Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects”). Consider merging to avoid redundancy and improve scannability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward; title casing is inconsistent (“Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT”); “Coleman DAVIS” may look visually inconsistent unless intentional. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language such as “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience to ground the summary, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Trim the long list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills section.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Combines strategic oversight with hands-on delivery across enterprise platforms, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia. Recently led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and is now shaping AI-enabled search and discovery for mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already signals leadership focus, so the intro does not need to restate broad capability lists.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Standardize style by avoiding “&” if other sections mostly use “and.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it shorter and more category-based.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more consistent will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line lead-in such as “Selected recent projects” and keep all entries in parallel past-tense structure.
- Tighten wording: “bill-level AI chat” → “AI chat at the bill level”; “continued campaign growth” → “future campaign expansion.”
- Emphasize outcomes or scope where possible: users, content volume, campaign audience, or organizational purpose.
- Consider this cleaner version:  
  **AI Hybrid Search:** Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite:** Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future expansion.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign:** Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display integrated with the main site.  
  **Advocacy Video Series:** Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video work are already reflected in Work Experience; keep this section shorter and more project-focused to avoid repetition.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives so it feels distinct from the NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “deliver,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: “Designed,” “Led,” “Built,” “Established,” “Improved.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 sharper points, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Established digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.
- Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search accuracy gains, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on consulting ownership and AI/search work.
- Microsite/campaign examples also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same project details verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact wins: website migration, analytics stack expansion, in-house studio build, governance/operations.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add team size, budget, traffic/email growth, production volume, reporting efficiency, or cost savings from the studio build and analytics improvements.
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize strategic ownership, not routine management: “Oversaw multi-channel communications reaching tens of thousands of county officials” rather than listing email/social generically.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version more strategic and less operational.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; focus here on building the studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinctly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the broader strategic remit of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s “governance” and “planning systems”; keep this version tactical, not strategic.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector advocacy storytelling and audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “storytelling” or “communications strategy” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- Keep phrasing parallel: use noun phrases only, avoid mixing broad themes with execution-level wording.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable proof points for experience bullets rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with NACo role bullets; keep this section high-level and let experience show the scale.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- SharePoint
- Power Pages

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop older/less central platforms here unless required by the role; keep WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages in “Technical + IT.”
- Remove “jQuery” from Topline Skills unless it is explicitly important for target roles; it reads dated versus your recent strategic/modernization work.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Drupal modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “enterprise CMS modernization and integration.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Looker Studio
- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” As a topline skills item, it should emphasize strategic analytics capability over repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and KPI design
- Executive and leadership reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity
- SEO, user behavior and performance analysis

- Tighten wording: replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, user behavior and performance analysis” if accurate.
- If you can support it elsewhere, align this with impact from recent roles: analytics infrastructure, decision support, and optimization for large-scale web platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list across sections; keep this section higher-level than Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with work experience that already proves studio and livestream capability. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent strengths and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera systems • Virtual event production”
- Lead with delivery-level skills (“broadcast,” “hybrid event delivery”) rather than task phrasing like “video production and editing.”
- Consider dropping “virtual event production” if space is tight; “livestream and hybrid event delivery” already implies it.
- If you can support it elsewhere, strengthen with scale/context language such as “broadcast-quality” to align with the NACo studio build.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are already substantiated by the NACo role; avoid expanding this section into a repeat of that bullet.
- “Multimedia & live event production” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this version concise and more specific.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should emphasize proficiency level or scope rather than repeat names.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the strongest, most recent platform: “Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; modular content builds)” to reinforce impact.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “GitHub Pages” or remove it if it was only lightly used.
- Consider trimming to the 3–4 platforms with meaningful professional use if GitHub Pages or Power Pages were secondary.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress in multiple skills sections unless this section adds context (scale, migration, architecture, governance).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles or reduced to avoid repeating topline skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied execution tools: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group by function for readability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Keep only tools you’ve used recently and can discuss concretely; if GTM is not central in recent roles, consider dropping it.
- Suggested rewrite: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • Tag management: Google Tag Manager”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and “workflow automation” themes already listed under Topline Skills.
- If space is tight, merge this into “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” rather than maintaining a separate near-duplicate section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” positioning elsewhere. Make it more selective and frame tools by function, emphasizing systems you’ve actually used to build workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools”
- Group by purpose for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Keep only tools tied to meaningful use; if Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier are the strongest, lead with those and consider dropping one or two generic PM tools.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of a pure list, e.g. “Used to build editorial workflows, intake systems, cross-team planning, and process automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are very common and low-signal unless they support a stronger systems story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, but it’s currently just a vendor list. Make it more specific and aligned to the scale/ownership already shown in your recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, Member Engagement & Journey Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Automated journeys
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools: campaign deployment, list management, or engagement reporting
- Keep platform names only if you’ve used them directly; otherwise remove weaker/older tools to avoid looking broad but shallow

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email” too many times since it already appears prominently across recent NACo roles and the summary
- Don’t add analytics terms here that are already covered under Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” This item should be tighter and more tool-focused, with methods/outcomes moved to recent experience bullets.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Data & Analytics Tools
- Replace with a cleaner tools-only list: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console
- Remove broader capability terms like SEO, A/B testing, and Dashboarding unless you add specificity elsewhere; they read as functions, not tools.
- If you want to keep optimization, make it more concrete: GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Search Console • Experimentation analysis

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly; consider keeping the fuller version there and shortening this to tools only.
- “Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure…” in the 2022–2024 role already carries the impact; avoid repeating capability claims here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft language: replace “high-impact digital content” with named deliverables like “livestreams, weekly advocacy videos, and multimedia web content.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided informal supervision and daily guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; specify early-stage process building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete ownership and outputs, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Condense the rest of the media work into one support clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and program outreach.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, or types/volume of research projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already cover web, video, and multimedia leadership in more depth.
- Don’t overstate strategic digital ownership here; keep focus on coordination, research support, and the podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it a tighter software/tools list and avoid restating capabilities already proven elsewhere.
